Season shape

Getting started

  1. Set the season up in Setup → Season, and paste your Terms & Conditions and Waiver in Communication → Sign-up form.
  2. Add your teams in Teams & players → Teams (eight for the standard format).
  3. In Communication → Sign-up form, say where registrations land, deploy the script and press Put the form on the link. That link is what you send the players.
  4. Approve them in Teams & players → Registrations — or import a returned code or file there by hand.
  5. Setup → Draw generates the season, then run each game from Match night → Live match.
  6. After the last round the semi-finals draw themselves; follow them in Competition → Finals. The winner goes to Stats & records → Honours.

Send history

1 · The web app

One Google Apps Script does both jobs for this competition: it holds the live page players look at, and it holds the shared copy every tablet reads and writes. Set it up once.
How to set it up, step by step
  1. Press Copy setup script.
  2. Open script.google.com → New project, select everything in the editor and paste over it.
  3. Deploy → New deployment, choose Web app. Execute as Me, who has access Anyone. Google will ask you to allow it — that is it asking for your own Drive.
  4. Copy the /exec address it gives you and paste it in the box above.
  5. Later, after an update to this tool: press Copy setup script again, paste it over the old code, then Deploy → Manage deployments → Edit (pencil) → Version: New version → Deploy. The address never changes.

2 · The live page

The page players and parents watch: the table, the fixtures, the results and the stats, at the same address all season. It is read-only — nobody can change anything from there.

3 · Share this league between tablets

This tablet runs the league Hand this code to the other tablet. It carries the address and the key — treat it like a password. Turn sharing on to get a code.
This tablet is joining one On the other tablet, open this tab, press Join a shared league and paste the code. It appears in the league switcher and starts syncing at once.
Every tablet keeps its own full copy, so a wifi drop never stops a match being scored — whatever was logged goes up when the signal comes back.
Putting the league on a second tablet, in order
  1. On this tablet: set the web app up above, then tick share this league.
  2. Press Copy the join code and send it to yourself — a message, an email, anything.
  3. On the other tablet: open the tool, sign in, and come to this same tab.
  4. Press Join a shared league and paste the code.
  5. Both now show the same league. Score on either; whatever one writes, the other picks up within a few seconds. Two referees should take different matches — the same match on two tablets at once is the one thing to avoid.

Where registrations land

Registration form builder

Tick more than one and the form asks the player which they are registering for. Their teams, terms, waiver and age limit follow that choice, and the submission lands in that competition's inbox — whichever league you have open when you import it.
The web app is the form. Each competition gets its own script: deploy it once, press Put the form on the link, and the /exec address opens the registration form itself. Submitting from there hands the registration straight to the script, which emails it to you with the signed .futreg attached — no hosting, no download, nothing for a player's computer to be suspicious of.

The downloaded file is the same form as a single self-contained HTML, for sending by hand or hosting somewhere else.

Whichever way it is delivered the player lands on a completion record showing what they signed, which they can print. A .futreg file and a paste-in code are always offered as a fallback — both import on the Registrations tab beside this one.

Rebuild and re-share the form after changing anything: the delivery address, the terms, the waiver and the team list are baked into the file each player has.

Terms & Conditions

Waiver / assumption of risk

Season

Leagues

Every league keeps its own players, teams, draw, table, stats, sign-up form and live page. Nothing crosses between them: somebody who turns out in two competitions is registered in each, and what they do in one is counted there alone.

People & access

How access works, and what it is not
Each person gets their own PIN of four to eight digits, and no two may share one. Open the arrow beside a name to give them a league. A referee can start a match, run the clock and log goals and cards; they cannot touch the draw, teams, registrations, exports or these settings, and they do not see players' contact details. A manager runs their league in full. The owner sees every league and is the only one who can add leagues or people.
This is role separation, not security. The PINs and every league are held in this browser, so anyone who opens the developer tools can read or change them. Use it to keep match-day duties separate — not as a lock on personal data. Once the leagues are shared from your Google Drive, the separation is enforced where the data lives rather than here.

Data

Everything is held in this browser on this machine. Take a .json backup regularly — clearing your browser data erases the league, and a backup is the only way back.
Backup to .jsonThe whole league in one file — teams, players, every result and the roll of honour. Keep one per match night.
Restore from .jsonPuts a backup back. Replaces what is in this league — the other competitions are left alone.
Export Excel workbookPlayers, table, results, scorers, discipline, attendance and the money, as sheets. For sending on, not for restoring.

Starting again

Both of these erase the competition you have open — its teams, its draw, every result and all of its players. Your other competitions, the people who sign in and the roll of honour of the other leagues are untouched. There is no undo: take a backup first.
Load the demo seasonEight teams, squads and a full draw to try the workflow on. It replaces this competition with the demo.
Erase this competitionWipes the lot and leaves an empty season. Your sign-up settings and live-page link are kept.
